title: Energy levels of screened charged impurity in gapped graphene under magnetic field
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive theoretical study of the electronic states in gapped graphene in the presence of a charge impurity and a magnetic field. We focus on the impurity-induced modification of the Landau levels under the influence of an attractive or repulsive Coulomb potential. Since analytical solutions of the Dirac equation are not available in this case, the study is carried out using the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approach. Special attention is paid to the screening of the Coulomb potential in the presence of metallic gates situated at some distances from graphene sheet, as is commonly the case in experiments. Using both analytical and numerical methods, we determine the energy spectrum as a function of the magnetic field strength and impurity charge for screened and unscreened Coulomb potentials. Our results reveal a significant dependence of the energy levels for sample-to-gate distances of less than 50 nm.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis of how charged impurities modify the Landau levels in gapped graphene under a magnetic field. It utilizes the WKB approximation to derive the energy spectrum, paying special attention to the screening effects introduced by nearby metallic gates. The results highlight that these gate-induced screening effects significantly alter the energy levels, especially at small sample-to-gate distances.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates the electronic energy levels within gapped graphene when subjected simultaneously to a charged impurity potential and a perpendicular magnetic field.
main_result: The energy spectrum exhibits a significant dependence on the screening distance between the sample and metallic gates, particularly for small distances (less than 50 nm).
method: The Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation is employed to solve the Dirac equation, leading to a generalized Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization condition that incorporates a geometric phase.
model_or_system: The system is gapped graphene modeled by a low-energy Dirac Hamiltonian, incorporating a screened Coulomb potential derived from polarization effects and nearby metallic gates.
key_observables: Energy spectrum (Landau levels) as a function of magnetic field strength and impurity charge.
important_parameters: Gap parameter (e.g., 53 meV), magnetic field strength (B), impurity charge (Z), and sample-to-gate distance (d).
main_assumptions: The WKB method is used due to the lack of exact analytical solutions, and the potential is modeled by a screened Coulomb potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of distorted energy levels on impurity charge and explicitly show the dependence of these levels on the screening distance (d).
paper_structure: The study progresses by first establishing the WKB method for general potentials, then focusing on the screened Coulomb potential model, followed by numerical results, and concluding with the physical implications.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of screening effects from nearby metallic gates provides a crucial, experimentally relevant refinement to standard theoretical models of impurity states in 2D Dirac materials.
